question: Among the earlier transesterification studies that the Aspen Plus biodiesel models are compared with, which reports the highest conversion, and at what reaction temperature and methanol-to-oil ratio?
expect: Gaurav et al. (2013): 99.38% at 160 °C, 9:1, 3 wt% CaO on Al2O3 (Table 11, p9)
rendered:
The document title "Engineering a GO-Gd2TiO5/g-C3N4 ternary nanocomposite for enhanced electrochemical performance and biodiesel catalysis" does not contain the information about earlier transesterification studies that the Aspen Plus biodiesel models are compared with.

However, the document title "Development of an Aspen Plus model for catalytic transesterification with different reactor arrangements and kinetic mechanisms" contains the information about the comparison with earlier studies.

In Table 11 of the document "Development of an Aspen Plus model for catalytic transesterification with different reactor arrangements and kinetic mechanisms", the study by Gaurav et al. (2013) reports a conversion of 99.38% at a reaction temperature of 160 °C and a methanol-to-oil ratio of 9:1.
